title: Hierarchical rerank evaluation infra for per-customer NDCG/MRR with latency bucketing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a hierarchical evaluation infrastructure to compute NDCG and MRR across multiple aggregation levels (global, customer, customer-segment, prompt-set) while correlating ranking quality with observed latency buckets. This ticket covers ingestion of customer prompt sets, an evaluation runner that supports per-customer scoring, latency-aware weighting, A/B testing hooks for traffic-split experiments, and backfill tooling for historical runs.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline ingests customer prompt sets (CSV/JSONL) and attaches metadata (customer_id, prompt_set_id, version).
Evaluation runner emits NDCG@k and MRR metrics at customer, segment, and global levels daily and on-demand runs.
Latency buckets are defined (0-50ms, 50-150ms, 150-500ms, 500ms+); evaluation output includes per-bucket metrics and weighted aggregate scores.
A/B hooks allow routing a configurable percentage of rerank traffic to alternative rankers and the runner associates trial buckets with metric deltas.
Backfill job supports running historical telemetry through the same eval codepath and stores results in the evaluations datastore for comparisons.
Schema changes for telemetry are backward-compatible; storage and cost remain within the approved budget envelope.
tasks: Spec: define hierarchical aggregation model and latency bucket boundaries (doc link in links).
Ingest: add prompt-set parser + validation into eval-ingest service with per-customer quotas.
Runner: implement per-customer NDCG/MRR calculation, support top-k truncation and ties handling.
Telemetry: extend rerank telemetry schema to include latency_ms and experiment_bucket tags.
A/B: add experiment tagging and traffic-split cookie/header instrumentation in the rerank proxy.
Backfill: author a backfill job that replays stored requests into the evaluation runner at sampling rate.
Dashboards: expose per-customer and per-bucket NDCG/MRR timeseries + delta overlays for AB experiments.
Docs & runbook: update runbook for interpreting latency-weighted quality regressions and thresholds for alerts.
decisions: Use discrete latency buckets instead of continuous modeling to reduce noise and storage costs; buckets chosen after sampling existing latency distribution.
Weighted aggregate score will penalize high-latency buckets by configurable factors to surface human-visible regressions even if global NDCG is stable.
Store full per-query scores only for sampled traffic (1%) and aggregate-only for the rest to keep telemetry costs tractable.
Adopt OpenTelemetry-compatible labels for experiment metadata to reuse existing tracing/observability systems.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Aisha K: Initial spec posted to Confluence; requested feedback from PM (Riley) and Design (June).
2026-02-25 - Riley Chen (PM): Asked to prioritize per-customer thresholds and to include SLA-linked alerts for high-latency regressions.
2026-03-01 - Engineering sync: agreed on buckets 0-50 / 50-150 / 150-500 / 500+. Mateo to prototype aggregation code by Mar 8.
2026-03-05 - PR review: infra/runner implementation shows 2x memory peak for full per-query retention; opted for sampled retention. See PR #482.
2026-03-10 - QA: Small discrepancy in MRR for ties; decided on stable tie-breaking (score then timestamp) in runner to keep results deterministic.
2026-03-12 - Mateo R: Canary instrumentation deployed to staging for 5% traffic. Observability confirms bucket tags present in traces.
notes: Sampling trade-off: storing every per-query vector for full analyses would increase storage by ~6x; agreed to sampled retention with deterministic sampling key (customer_id + day).
Privacy: prompt-set ingestion must obey redaction rules in privacy runbook; implement a validation step to enforce PII filters before storage.
Rollout plan: start with internal canary customers, expand to <10 pilot customers, then GA once runbook and dashboards validated.
